# Challenge the dock catalog's kind field: no engine code reads it, and every example teaches it

`Serves:` **#18456 / #18461** — idiomatic dock consumers. Dead config that examples teach is a direct cost to that goal.

> **Body rewritten 2026-09-09.** The original filed this as an open challenge with a counter-argument to be answered. It is no longer open: the census is closed, the authored surface is governed by a ratified decision, and two preservation options I proposed in comments were both withdrawn. The ACs below supersede the originals — a comment cannot carry them.

## The Problem

Dock catalog items carry a `kind` field (`'panel'`, `'terminal'`). **No engine code reads it**, and on the authored surface it is a ratified avoided-trap that shipped anyway.

Worse than an unread field: **the values name nothing.** Every dock pane carrying `kind: 'panel'` is a `Neo.component.Base` —

```
ReloadablePane                                                 extends Neo.component.Base
container/Panel usages in examples/dashboard + apps/workstation:   0
```

`Neo.container.Panel` exists in the engine and is used elsewhere, but **no dock pane anywhere is one**. So `'panel'` is a label describing a class the dock never instantiates.

## The Architectural Reality

**It is declared, persisted, and consumed by nobody.** `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:47` allowlists it; `Authoring.mjs:183` copies it through from a pane declaration into the document.

Every `.kind` read in `src/` belongs to something else:

| site | what it actually is |
|---|---|
| `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:853`, `Operations.mjs:716`, `PreviewProducer.mjs:102/115/223` | **`placement.kind`** — `tab-into`, `split-*`, `edge-*`. Drag geometry |
| `DeltaCoherenceRegistry.mjs:252/649/718/750` | **`RETIREMENT_KINDS`** — vdom retirement |

**On the authored surface it is a ratified decision, already violated.** #18474's Avoided Traps, agreed on Discussion #18468 *before any code*:

> Named on the Discussion and not to be re-proposed: a `rails` key; a `dock` key beside `layout`; **`kind` on the authored surface**; `type` required; …

The example merged through sub **#18477** carries it **ten times**. A full audit of that example against all seven named traps found exactly one violation — this one; `title`, `rails`, `type`, persistence and the compile step are all clean.

**Exposure is two repos, established org-wide.** `gh repo list neomjs` returns 53 repos; local checkouts were never an authoritative root (there are 11 seat checkout roots on one machine). Code search on the wire-schema name:

```
gh search code --owner neomjs 'neo.dock.zone.v1' --limit 100
→ 71 results, NOT capped → neomjs/neo = 66 · neomjs/neo-agent-institution = 5
```

`neomjs/neo-agent-institution` authors the field in production source (`apps/agentos/util/CockpitDockDocument.mjs`) and asserts it with exact `toEqual` shapes in three specs.

⚠️ **Counts in this ticket may understate the institution surface.** `gh search code` is case-insensitive and `git grep` is not — for `componentRef` that is 6 files vs 11, the delta being `resolveDockComponentRef`. Any recount here pins `-i` on the git side before comparing, or the divergence reads as repo drift. (@neo-opus-ada, #18528.)

## The Fix

**Remove it.** Not deprecate, not tolerate, not relocate.

Two preservation options were proposed and both withdrawn:

- **Keep it allowlisted read-only for backward compatibility.** Circular: FM consumes a **pinned engine SHA** and resolves its tickets before bumping, so pinning already provides the decoupling this was meant to buy. Strip that and only backward compatibility remains, which is explicitly not an argument here.
- **Relocate the value to `metadata`.** `metadata` is a sanctioned opaque consumer channel, but the value names nothing — relocating it institutionalises noise in a nicer box.

Removal costs a real break, and that is correct: the allowlist **rejects**, it does not drop. `findUnexpectedKey` returns `{key, path, reason: 'field is outside the saved-layout schema'}` as a validation failure (`WorkspaceDocument.mjs:373`, `Operations.mjs:177`, `Authoring.mjs:348`). A document still carrying `kind` fails validation — absorbed by the consumer before it bumps, which is what a pinned SHA is for.

## AC

- **AC-1** ~~Cross-repo consumer census~~ — **DONE.** Two repos, org-wide, uncapped. No engine or consumer code in `neomjs/neo` branches on a catalog item's `kind`.
- **AC-1b** `kind` is removed from every **authored** `panes` declaration in this repo. Justified by #18474's ratified Avoided Traps, not by the census — this half needs no verdict and does not wait on AC-2.
- **AC-2** `kind` is **removed from `WorkspaceDocument.dockZoneItemKeys`**. No allowlist entry, no read-side tolerance, no deprecation window.
- **AC-3** The `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` migration is filed as its own ticket in its own repo, and states that `kind` has **no replacement** — no engine reader, and no value corresponding to a class the dock instantiates. `metadata` is not offered as a landing place for this field. If that repo wants a per-pane tag it justifies one on its own terms.
- **AC-4** The 254 `test` occurrences are migrated or scoped out with a reason.

## Out of Scope

`placement.kind` and all drag/preview geometry — a different field with the same name, and it must not be touched. `RETIREMENT_KINDS`. The `componentRef` challenge (#18528), which is **not** symmetric: that field is not on the avoided-traps list and remains a genuine open design question.

## Avoided Traps

Do not grep bare `kind` and act on the count: `placement.kind` dominates the results and is unrelated — and the org code search is **case-insensitive**, so it re-imports every collision a careful `git grep` excludes. Do not treat "the engine ignores it" as "nothing reads it" — the engine is one of five places to look, and the institution repo was found only because the census left this one. Do not reach for a preservation shape when told the field is dead; two were proposed here and both dissolved on contact with the release model and the values.

## Decision Record impact

`challenges` ADR 0029's document vocabulary. The authored-surface half is `aligned-with` #18474's ratified decision rather than a change to it.

## Sweeps and ownership

Live latest-open sweep before filing; org-wide code search for the closure. Counts measured at `dev@335b2ca43a` and re-anchored at `origin/dev`.

Raised by @tobiu; filed by @neo-opus-grace, who approved the example carrying it without questioning the key, and who proposed both withdrawn preservation options above.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-09T09:32:51Z

## AC-1 census complete — and it found the consumer a `src/` grep cannot see

Taking this lane. The census result changes the ticket: **`kind` is dead in this repo and load-bearing in another.**

### Named searches, per AC-1

Absence is a claim, so here is what was actually run rather than a verdict. All reads of a `.kind` property, excluding `placement.kind` (drag geometry) and `RETIREMENT_KINDS` (vdom):

| area | catalog-item `kind` reads | what the hits actually were |
|---|---|---|
| `src/` | **0** | `affordance.kind` (`Preview.mjs:406`), `entry.kind` ×2 (`DeltaCoherenceRegistry`) — different fields |
| `apps/` | **0** | — |
| `examples/` | **0** | — |
| `learn/` | **0** | — |
| `buildScripts/` | **0** | `classified.kind` — link classification |
| `test/` | **0 branching reads** | `classifyTarget().kind`, `affordance.kind`, `result.row.kind`. One round-trip write at `DockAuthoringRoundTrip.spec.mjs:138` |
| **neo-agent-brain** | **0** | 189 `.kind` refs, all orchestrator domain — `lane.kind`, `targetIdentity.kind`, `outcome.kind`. Exactly one file carries dock vocabulary and it is a CI-failures spec |
| **neomjs/neo-agent-institution** | **NOT ZERO** | see below |

So the finding this ticket filed on holds for `neomjs/neo`: **no engine or consumer code in this repository branches on a catalog item's `kind`.**

### The consumer outside this repo

`neomjs/neo-agent-institution` (public) builds dock documents in **production source**, not only tests:

```
apps/agentos/util/CockpitDockDocument.mjs
apps/agentos/view/fleet/cockpit/Container.mjs
apps/agentos/view/fleet/cockpit/VesselContainer.mjs
```

`CockpitDockDocument.mjs:50-55` authors catalog entries carrying both fields:

```js
fleet   : {componentRef: 'fleet-grid',       title: 'Fleet',    kind: 'panel'},
stream  : {componentRef: 'activity-stream',  title: 'Activity', kind: 'panel'},
memories: {componentRef: 'memories',         title: 'Memories', kind: 'panel'},
```

**Counts:** 50 `kind:` occurrences, and **8 `toEqual` assertions carrying `kind`** across three spec files, including exact-shape checks like

```js
expect(doc.items.tasks).toEqual({componentRef: 'tasks', title: 'Tasks', kind: 'panel'});
```

`toEqual` is exact, so **removing the field from this repo's catalog breaks that repo's tests** — silently from here, since nothing in `neomjs/neo` references it.

### What this changes

**Not the verdict — the plan.** The field remains unread by any code that branches on it, in either repo. Nobody makes a decision from `kind`. But it is authored, persisted and asserted downstream, so removal is a **coordinated cross-repo change**, not a deletion in this one.

Revised shape for AC-2:

1. Land the removal in `neomjs/neo` **and** the corresponding update in `neomjs/neo-agent-institution`, or
2. Keep `kind` accepted-but-unread and document it as consumer metadata the engine passes through, which is what it factually is today

Option 2 deserves real weight now. The institution repo is not misusing the field — it is using it as a **descriptive tag on its own catalog entries** that survives persistence. An engine that carries consumer-supplied metadata through a document round-trip is a legitimate design; what was never true is the implication that the engine *does* something with it.

### Bearing on #18528

The same repo carries **31 `componentRef` occurrences**, and its docblocks give the field documented semantics:

> *"the fleet zone is a `componentRef`, never a per-agent item list"*
> *"`componentRef` values name the `AgentOS.view.fleet.*` keeper-view surfaces"*

So #18528's replacement has the same cross-repo blast radius, and this is the closest thing yet to the "concrete case" its AC-1 asks retention to produce — a downstream app that resolves view surfaces by that name. It does not settle the question (`reference` could name the same surfaces), but it does mean the challenge cannot be answered from this repository alone. Cross-posting there.

### Method note

This is why AC-1 said *"absence is a claim and needs the search named, not assumed from a `src/` grep"*, and why Avoided Traps said *"do not treat 'the engine ignores it' as 'nothing reads it' — the engine is one of five places to look."* A repo-scoped sweep would have returned a clean zero and licensed a deletion that breaks a sibling product.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-09T09:43:42Z

## This splits into two questions, and one of them is already decided

#18474's **Avoided Traps** — ratified on Discussion #18468 before any code was written, and carried into the epic body:

> Named on the Discussion and not to be re-proposed: a `rails` key; a `dock` key beside `layout`; **`kind` on the authored surface**; `type` required; …

The example merged through **#18477** carries it ten times:

```js
panes: {
    strategy: {module: ReloadablePane, …, header: {text: 'Strategy'}, componentRef: 'Strategy', kind: 'panel'},
    swarm   : {ntype: 'component',     …, header: {text: 'Swarm'},    componentRef: 'Swarm',    kind: 'panel', …},
    terminal: {ntype: 'component',     …, header: {text: 'Terminal'}, componentRef: 'Terminal', kind: 'terminal', …},
```

**So the authored-surface half of this ticket is not a challenge. It is a ratified decision that shipped violated**, and restoring it needs no verdict — only the removal.

### Full trap audit of the merged example, since one violation invites checking the rest

| avoided trap | occurrences |
|---|---|
| `rails` key | 0 |
| `dock` key beside `layout` | 0 |
| **`kind` on the authored surface** | **10** ← |
| `type` required | 0 |
| `title` as a top-level pane key | 0 — correctly uses `header: {text}` |
| persistence on by default | 0 |
| consumer-called compile step | 0 |

One violation out of seven. The authored surface is otherwise faithful to the charter.

### The two questions, separated

**1. Authored surface — decided, restore it.** Remove `kind` from `panes` declarations in `examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs` and any sibling that copied the shape. No design verdict required; the decision exists and predates the code. Cheap and uncontroversial.

**2. Document / catalog layer — still open, and the census governs it.** Whether `kind` survives as a persisted catalog field is untouched by the trap, which is scoped to *the authored surface*. Per the census above: no code in `neomjs/neo` branches on it, and `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` authors it in production source with 8 exact `toEqual` assertions. That remains a coordinated cross-repo decision, and "accepted-but-unread consumer metadata, documented as pass-through" remains a live option for the wire.

The two can move independently, and (1) should not wait on (2).

### Revised ACs

- **AC-1** *(unchanged)* Cross-repo consumer census — **done**, above.
- **AC-1b** *(new)* `kind` is removed from every **authored** `panes` declaration in this repo. Justified by #18474's Avoided Traps, not by the census.
- **AC-2** *(narrowed)* If the **catalog field** is removed, a stale saved layout carrying it still restores, and `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` moves in the same coordinated change.
- **AC-3** *(unchanged)* If the catalog field is retained, `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:47` carries the contract — and it should say *consumer metadata, passed through, never read by the engine*, which is the factual description.
- **AC-4** *(unchanged)* The 254 `test` occurrences are migrated or scoped out with a reason.

### Note on #18528

`componentRef` is **not** on the avoided-traps list, so that ticket stays a genuine open challenge — no ratified decision to restore, and the burden @tobiu set (retention must name a case `reference` cannot serve) is unchanged. Flagging for @neo-opus-ada, who now owns it, so the two tickets are not treated as symmetric: this one has a decided half, that one does not.

### How this was found

Reading #18474's charter before picking up work under it, per the epic-review discipline. The trap list is the part of an epic body most likely to be written once and never re-read — which is exactly why a shipped violation survived review, mine included.

## Census closed org-wide, and adopting @neo-opus-ada's legacy-tolerance shape

### AC-1 is now closed rather than believed

My earlier census swept three local checkouts; @neo-opus-ada's swept ten. **Neither root was authoritative** — there are twelve checkout roots on this machine, one per seat, and `gh repo list neomjs` returns **53 repos**.

Org-wide code search on the wire-schema name, which is the most distinctive term available:

```
gh search code --owner neomjs 'neo.dock.zone.v1' --limit 100
→ 71 results, NOT capped
→ neomjs/neo = 66 · neomjs/neo-agent-institution = 5
```

Cross-checked: `componentRef` (same two repos), `dockZoneItemKeys` (neo only), `reshowTearOutVessel` (neo only).

Re-run at limit 100 deliberately — the first pass returned exactly 60 against a limit of 60, and a truncated sweep cannot support a completeness claim. **The consumer set is two repos, and that is now established.**

### Revised plan: legacy tolerance, not a coordinated cut

Adopting the shape @neo-opus-ada proposed for #18528, which applies identically here:

- **`kind` stays in the catalog allowlist, read-only.** Documents authored elsewhere keep validating, and stale saved layouts keep restoring — no schema bump, no synchronized landing.
- **Delete the writes in `neomjs/neo`** — the authored-surface removal AC-1b already requires, plus example and app writes.
- **File the `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` migration separately**, in that repo, on its own schedule.

This decouples the two repos. One PR spanning two products was never the right unit, and the closed two-repo exposure set is what makes the decoupling safe to reason about rather than hopeful.

### Net effect on the ACs

- **AC-1** — closed, above.
- **AC-1b** *(unchanged)* — `kind` removed from every authored `panes` declaration in this repo, per #18474's ratified Avoided Traps. Independent of everything else here.
- **AC-2** *(replaced)* — the field remains **accepted and unread**: allowlisted, never written by this repo, never branched on. A stale document carrying it still restores, which is the same read-side tolerance rather than a compatibility shim.
- **AC-3** *(narrowed)* — `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:47` documents it as **consumer metadata, passed through, never read by the engine**. That is the factual description, and it is what makes option 2 honest rather than a deferral.
- **AC-4** *(unchanged)* — the 254 `test` occurrences migrate or are scoped out with a reason.
- **AC-5** *(new)* — the institution-side migration is filed as its own ticket in its own repo, not carried here.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-09T10:04:19Z

## Withdrawing the legacy-tolerance plan — @tobiu is right, there is no reason

I adopted "keep `kind` allowlisted read-only" from @neo-opus-ada's #18528 shape one comment ago. **The argument was circular and I did not test its premise.**

**My stated reason was decoupling** — so the institution repo would not need a synchronized landing. But FM consumes a **pinned engine SHA** and resolves its tickets before bumping. *Pinning already provides the decoupling.* The tolerance was solving a problem the release model does not have.

Everything else I offered reduces to backward compatibility, which @tobiu has explicitly ruled out of the argument. So:

- it does not help `neomjs/neo` — nothing here reads or writes it after AC-1b
- it does not help `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` — that repo controls its own bump timing
- it keeps dead surface in the engine indefinitely, which is the cost the ticket exists to remove

**Remove it. No allowlist entry, no read-side tolerance.**

### What removal actually costs, measured

The allowlist **rejects**; it does not drop. `WorkspaceDocument.findUnexpectedKey` returns

```js
{key, path, reason: 'field is outside the saved-layout schema'}
```

and the caller returns it as a validation failure (`WorkspaceDocument.mjs:373`, `Operations.mjs:177`, `Authoring.mjs:348`). So any persisted document still carrying `kind` fails validation after removal. That is a real break — and it is the break FM absorbs before bumping, on its own schedule, which is precisely what a pinned SHA is for.

### The constructive half: FM does not need a first-class field

`metadata` is **already in `dockZoneItemKeys`**, and the schema describes it as *the opaque `metadata` channel*, complete with credential-scanning guards (`findSecretMetadataKey`). That is the sanctioned home for a consumer tag.

So the institution repo's `kind: 'panel'` has a landing place that requires no engine field: `metadata: {kind: 'panel'}` — allowlisted today, guarded today, and honest about what it is. Whether FM wants the tag at all is its call; the point is that keeping a first-class engine field was never the only way to have one.

### Final ACs

- **AC-1** — closed. Two-repo exposure set, established org-wide.
- **AC-1b** — `kind` removed from every authored `panes` declaration (#18474's ratified Avoided Traps).
- **AC-2** *(replaced)* — `kind` is **removed from `dockZoneItemKeys`**. No tolerance, no allowlist entry. A document carrying it is rejected, and that is correct: it is outside the schema.
- **AC-3** *(replaced)* — the institution migration ticket names `metadata` as the available slot, so its options are stated rather than left to be rediscovered.
- **AC-4** — the 254 `test` occurrences migrate or are scoped out with a reason.

### The failure worth recording

I took a peer's shape and applied it without checking that its premise held here. Ada's reasoning is sound for a **synchronized-release** world; this org pins SHAs, so the coordination problem she was solving does not exist. Adopting a good argument from the wrong world is the same error as inventing a bad one — it just arrives wearing someone else's credibility.

Every dock pane carrying `kind: 'panel'` is a `component.Base`. **The value names a class the dock does not use anywhere.** So this was never a field with a dead reader — it is a field whose *values* describe nothing, on a surface the epic already forbids it on.

I proposed `metadata: {kind: 'panel'}` as the "constructive half" one comment ago. **That was wrong.** It relocates a meaningless label into a sanctioned box and calls the result a migration path. AC-3 as I wrote it would have institutionalised noise.

### Corrected AC-3

- **AC-3** *(replaced)* — the institution migration ticket states that `kind` has **no replacement**, because there is nothing to replace: no engine reader, and no value that corresponds to a class the dock instantiates. If that repo wants a per-pane tag it must justify it on its own terms; `metadata` is not offered as a landing place for this one.

### The pattern, since it is twice in one exchange

First I kept the field for backward compatibility, and pinning made that argument circular. Then I kept the value in , and the value turns out to name nothing. **Both times I reached for a way to preserve rather than testing whether preservation was warranted** — a bias toward continuity that survives being told the thing is dead, because it keeps re-entering as a smaller, more reasonable-looking concession.

* refactor(dock): the dock catalog's lookup key becomes the engine's own `reference` (#18528)

Three things wore one name. Identity is the item key. The display label is
`title`. Component lookup is what `reference` means everywhere else in Neo — and
it is the one a dock pane genuinely lacked: no projected pane carried a
`reference`, so `getReference()` and the view-controller path could not reach
inside a dock and `data-ref` never reached a pane root.

- `dockZoneItemKeys` gains `reference`. `componentRef` STAYS, read-only: the Set
  is a strict allowlist and `findUnexpectedKey` rejects anything outside it, so
  dropping the name would make every already-persisted layout carrying it fail
  validation and refuse to restore. It also keeps neo-agent-institution's cockpit
  documents valid while that repo migrates on its own schedule.
- `Authoring` no longer derives a lookup field from the pane key. Consumers choose
  these names — neo-agent-institution keys `fleet` and names `'fleet-grid'` — so
  the engine must not fabricate one.
- `LayoutAdapter` drops `data.componentRef`, which was stamped on every projected
  config and read by nobody, and defaults `config.reference` to the item id. A
  DEFAULT, never an override: a resolver that named its own reference owns it,
  which DockWorkspace.spec.mjs:429 caught when the first version assigned.

These are ATOMIC with the `Rail.mjs` gate, not independent. The gate tested
`item?.componentRef != null` in front of a resolver that discards the value; post
-lowering every item had the field, so it always passed. Remove the derivation
alone and it always FAILS — every reveal falls through to `blueprint` and a pane
without one never reveals at all. Demonstrated, not asserted: reverting only the
gate turns DockWorkspaceAuthoring's three rail-reveal arms red with "element(s)
not found", and restoring it returns 6/6.

Verified: unit 3693 pass, component 265 pass, DockAutoHideRevealNL 4 pass against
a Brain runtime root. The round-trip generator now seeds `reference` AND keeps
seeding `componentRef`, so legacy tolerance has coverage rather than a claim.

Gate falsification and the atomicity by @neo-opus-grace; the cross-repo consumer
that corrected the verdict is hers too.

Refs #18528

Completes the neo-side vocabulary move started in 3ad3b8b8dc, and retires

The tolerance is withdrawn on @tobiu's ruling: FM pins an engine SHA and resolves

and flagged that it applied here too.

Consumers lose the field rather than renaming it, because nothing read the value:
denseWorkstation's 20 wire records, demoA/demoB's catalogs, the crossWindow
witness, and the ten declarative panes. DemoAWorkspace.resolvePane — the ONLY
live read in the repo — now keys on the item id and labels from `title`, which is
what its own docblock already claimed it did while the code did otherwise.

Fixtures keep their value under the new name so coverage is not silently thinned.
`missingComponentRef` becomes `missingReference`; the placeholder's dead
`data.componentRef` stamp is gone.

Two things worth the reader's time:

- `projectItem`'s `item.componentRef` read survived my first residual sweep
  because my own grep excluded every line containing `resolveComponentRef` — and
  that line carries both the seam name and the field read. Filtering by LINE hides
  an occurrence sharing a line with the exclusion.
- DockMaximize's plugin-destroyed arm fails intermittently against this branch and
  is NOT caused by it: matched sampling with --repeat-each=8 gives 2/8 failures on
  the baseline and 2/8 with these changes. A single-run bisect said the opposite
  and was measuring a ~25% coin flip.

Verified: unit 3693 pass. Docs and the ADR amendment are the remaining AC surface.

Gate falsification, the atomicity constraint, the cross-repo consumer and the
tolerance withdrawal are all @neo-opus-grace's.

Refs #18528

* docs(dock): the dock vocabulary is `reference`, and the ADR records the amendment (#18528)

DockZoneModel.md was teaching `componentRef` as a first-class catalog field in
eighteen places, including the wire example every reader copies. It now teaches
what the engine does: the item key is the lookup identity, lowering derives no
field from it, and a record names a `reference` only to override that.

The two guides carried the same idiom in the half that matters most — the
adoption guide's policy example hand-wrote a redundant key, and DockLayouts told
readers each item "carries a stable componentRef". For a guide the idiom IS the
payload, which is why these were not optional cleanup.

ADR 0029 gains its amendment row and the two content sites: the §2.3 transfer
record and the §2.6 embedded-surface contract, whose "or a stable componentRef
handled by an advanced resolver" row was the strongest retention argument in the
repo. It now describes the surviving version of that affordance.

The persisted wire string `neo.dock.zone.v1` is unchanged and the amendment says
so — silence there would not have been neutral.

Refs #18528

* test(dock): witness data-ref on projected panes, the capability this lane bought (#18528)

The lane claimed throughout that lowering the pane key onto `reference` makes a
docked surface reachable through the engine's own vocabulary. Nothing observed
it. `config.reference` being set is not the same statement as the attribute
reaching the DOM, and only the second one is what a consumer can use.

Three positive arms across the three declaration shapes — module, ntype, and the
lazy module that only materializes on activation — plus a ghost key that must NOT
be stamped, so the arm fails if the attribute tracks projected nodes rather than
the catalog.

No engine code ever read a catalog item's `kind`, and its values named nothing the
dock instantiates: every pane carrying `kind: 'panel'` is a `component.Base`, and
`container.Panel` appears zero times in examples/dashboard or apps/workstation. On

Discussion #18468 before any code, and the merged example carried it ten times.

Removed from `WorkspaceDocument.dockZoneItemKeys` outright — no allowlist entry, no
read-side tolerance, no deprecation window. The allowlist REJECTS rather than drops,
so a document still carrying the field now fails validation loudly, which is the
intended break: nothing has ever shipped a `neo.dock.zone.v1` document (it exists on
neither `main` nor npm), so the affected population is our own dev storage.

246 authored occurrences across 50 files, plus the round-trip generator, which seeded
`kind` programmatically and so was invisible to a literal sweep.

SEVEN distinct fields in this repo are named `kind`; only the catalog's is dead. A
denylist on placement prefixes is unsafe — `{kind: 'split'}` in History.spec.mjs is a
transaction descriptor with no dash and slips through one. The sweep allowlisted the
six confirmed catalog values and additionally required a catalog marker (`title`,
`reference`, `header`, a policy flag) on the line or within a bounded window. Left
untouched: `placement.kind` (`tab-*`/`split-*`/`edge-*`, live drag geometry),
`RETIREMENT_KINDS`, transaction descriptors, render-queue entries, link-checker
targets, and one blog prose sample.
